verdict.rationale: Trigger.dev's architecture is explicitly built on checkpoint-resume durability so tasks 'run normal TypeScript with no determinism constraints' and survive infrastructure issues; docs describe automatic retries with backoff, waitpoint tokens that pause/resume runs, version-locking so in-flight runs aren't affected by new deploys, and durable AI chats explicitly 'surviving refreshes, deploys, and crashes.' A community reference (Magic Patterns) also confirms real-world resilience where a custom process crashed under load but Trigger.dev jobs 'just worked.' Missing for 10: independent/hands-on verification of an actual mid-run crash-and-resume test and more detail on exactly how much step-level state is preserved versus re-executed.
